ethos.title: One essay a week. Nothing else.
ethos.p1: Every Monday, The Dailicle takes a single idea – about the mind, about meaning, about money, about the odd business of being a person – and follows it carefully, in plain language, at a length you can actually finish.
ethos.p2: There is no feed here and nothing to sign up for. You read the essay, you close the tab, and with a little luck the idea follows you around for the rest of the week.

meta.title: Why Read The Dailicle? A Manifesto for the Slow Web
meta.description: A rebellion against the noise of the internet. The philosophy behind one essay a week.

manifesto.title: Why Read Dailicle?
manifesto.subtitle: A manifesto for the slow web.
manifesto.p_library: The internet was supposed to be a library. Instead, it became a casino.
manifesto.p_scroll: Think about the last hour you spent scrolling. Can you remember one thing from it? The feeds are engineered by some of the smartest people alive to keep your thumb moving, and they are very good at their jobs. What they take is subtle: the evening feels full while the mind stays empty.
manifesto.p_rebellion: The Dailicle is a rebellion against that.
manifesto.p_one_1: We publish exactly one essay a week. Not ten. Not a feed. One, every Monday.
manifesto.p_one_2: Scarcity is a form of respect. When there is only one thing to read, you stop skimming and start reading. You give it your full attention, and we give it a full week of care: each essay is chosen from dozens of candidate ideas, researched properly, and written to be finished. Most take ten to fifteen minutes. There is a narration if you would rather listen.
manifesto.p_about_1: Five strands: psychology, philosophy, perspectives, life, and money. What connects them is a certain kind of idea – a specific, human observation you half-recognize but have never put into words. The worries you inherited from your parents. Why some days vanish and others last forever. What it quietly costs to keep every option open.
manifesto.p_about_2: A good essay here should still be on your mind on Wednesday.
manifesto.p_who_1: The curious. People who still believe a well-crafted sentence can change how you see the world, and people who suspect they would read more if reading felt less like homework. There is no signup, no paywall, and nothing to keep track of – one essay, once a week, free.
manifesto.p_who_2: If you want content to fill the silence, plenty of places will happily oblige. If you want ideas that linger after the tab closes, welcome home.
manifesto.p_writes: The Dailicle is run by one person. AI tools help draft essays and automate parts of translation, audio, and publishing. The weekly release is automated, and a human review before publication is not guaranteed. If you spot an error, please tell us so it can be corrected.
manifesto.p_recs_1: Recommendation algorithms are built for engagement, not enlightenment. We want you to read, think, and then leave. Go for a walk. Talk to a friend. Build something.
manifesto.p_recs_2: Sometimes an essay ends with a few pointers for anyone who wants to sit with the idea longer. But we will never trap you in a loop.
manifesto.closing: Read slowly. Think deeply. Come back Monday.

support.aboutIntro: The essays are free, with no paywall or ads. One person runs the publication, using AI tools to help draft essays and automate parts of publishing, translation, and audio. The weekly release is automated; a pre-publication human review is not guaranteed.
support.aboutPurpose: Reader contributions help pay for hosting, writing tools, translation, audio, and delivery. They make it easier to keep the archive and new essays open to everyone.
support.aboutHonesty: There is no public supporter count or funding target here because those numbers would need reliable accounting and context. Contributions are optional and do not buy a subscription or special access.
support.aboutCorrections: Found an error or have a question about an essay? Write to read@dailicle.com. Corrections and reader feedback matter more than pretending every issue is flawless.
